sources.title: TN MAWS Policy Note (annual, April budget session)
sources.publisher: TN Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department

provenance.note: Status changes only with a dated citation; per-commitment citations inline (commitment_source + status_history entries). update_model names the April MAWS Policy Note, ADB project documents and dated press as the re-check set.

headline: 16 commitments on Chennai's register: 4 delivered - including two big treatment plants - 3 on track, and 9 waiting on dates their owners set.
intro: Dated commitments by the institutions that manage this city's water - CMWSSB, the MAWS department, the state government and the courts that set deadlines for them - made to residents, courts and funders, and followed from announcement to delivery. Every commitment carries its original citation and every status change carries a dated source. Delivered late is still delivered - the dates show the journey - and when a date moves, the old one stays on the record. Nothing here is our opinion; it is the institutions' own paper, checked against time.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated timeline has not lapsed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: 100% metering of high-rise and commercial connections by 2023; 80% of domestic by 2027
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB Board (Metering Policy resolution of 23 November 2022, under the World Bank Chennai City Partnership)
commitments.what: CMWSSB's own board-approved metering policy set two targets: every high-rise and commercial connection metered by 2023, and 80% of ordinary domestic connections by 2027. As of May 2025, 3.12% of the city's 7.7 lakh connections had functioning meters (24,095). A 1-lakh smart-meter DBFOT package was announced with tender expected May 2025 and two-year installation, and the commercial/high-rise ambition quietly re-based to 90% by 2025-26. The same policy note carries an undated goal of cutting non-revenue water below 15%.

commitment_source.label: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.357 (CMWSSB Metering Policy, board resolution 23 Nov 2022)

status_history.note: Only 3.12% of 7.7 lakh connections metered (24,095 functioning meters), two and a half years after the policy and 17 months past the high-rise/commercial deadline. CMWSSB announces a 1-lakh smart-meter package (73,000 domestic in large buildings + 27,000 commercial/institutional), tender expected May 2025, with slab tariffs of Rs 6-45 per kilolitre.

The 1-lakh smart-meter package finally has a concessionaire: JWIL Infra, Rs 273.60 crore under a hybrid annuity model. Meter fixing expected to begin by December 2026 (itself a year later than the December 2025 start reported in November 2025) and the metering network to be completed by August 2028 - five years after the policy's original 2023 deadline for high-rises and commercial connections.

commitments.title: Perur 400 MLD desalination plant by December 2026
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu; JICA-funded; built by VA Tech Wabag + Metito
commitments.what: Chennai's fourth and largest desal plant: 400 MLD at Perur on East Coast Road, for ~22.67 lakh people in south Chennai and Tambaram. Foundation stone laid by CM M.K. Stalin on 21-22 August 2023; the 42-month EPC contract implied completion by December 2026. Since February 2026 the official line is commissioning by March 2027, with trial runs from around September 2026. Cost appears as Rs 4,276 crore (the plant contract) and Rs 6,078 crore (the full sanctioned project including the 59 km transmission main to Porur) - both are correct at different scopes.

commitment_source.label: Business Standard, 21 Aug 2023 (foundation stone); Dec 2026 target per Indian Infrastructure, 25 Jan 2024

status_history.note: Construction reaches 42% completion.

Around 62% complete; trial run expected by September 2026; completion revised to March 2027. CMWSSB MD T.G. Vinay separately put it at 'around 60%' with commissioning 'by March 2027' (DT Next, 11 Feb 2026).

commitments.title: Nemmeli II 150 MLD desalination plant by December 2021
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu; KfW + AMRUT funded; built by Cobra-Tecton consortium
commitments.what: Chennai's third desal plant: 150 MLD inside the existing Nemmeli campus with a ~47.6 km conveyance line to Pallavaram, for ~9 lakh people in south Chennai. Contract awarded 27 May 2019 (Rs 1,689 crore including 20-year O&M) with completion promised by December 2021. It was inaugurated on 24 February 2024 - roughly 26 months late, the date having moved three times through government documents on the way.

commitment_source.label: Contract award to Cobra-Tecton, 27 May 2019, completion Dec 2021 (DMS Universe project record; corroborated by CMWSSB's own project document recording the Dec-2021 pipeline contract horizon)

status_history.note: Government's own National Infrastructure Pipeline portal revises expected completion to 27 April 2023.
status_history.source_label: India Investment Grid (NIP project 607750), status updated 28 Mar 2022

status_history.note: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24 says the scheme is 'expected to be completed by July 2023'.
Inaugurated by CM M.K. Stalin - about 26 months after the original contract date.

commitments.title: Revamp the Minjur 100 MLD desalination plant (no date given)
commitments.what: Minjur was India's first large desal plant: promised for January 2009 under a 2005 concession with Chennai Water Desalination Ltd, delivered ~18 months late in July 2010 after cyclone damage. By 2025 output and quality had 'deteriorated considerably' and CMWSSB terminated the operator's contract - a decade before the concession's 2035 end. The board has promised a revamp: a consultant-led assessment 'within 30 days' of appointment and a DPR. It has published no date for when north Chennai gets its 100 MLD back. A promise without a due date is still a promise; this entry tracks it.

commitment_source.label: DT Next, 5 Jul 2025 ('Chennai Metro Water Board plans to revamp Minjur desalination plant')

status_history.note: The termination is on court record: in Madras High Court Section 9 proceedings, CMWSSB states it terminated CWDL's contract and seeks to take possession of the Kattupalli/Minjur plant and run it itself.
status_history.source_label: Madras HC Section 9 proceeding, CMWSSB v Chennai Water Desalination Ltd (~Mar 2025, via Casemine)

status_history.note: CMWSSB confirms it terminated the CWDL contract after output and quality deteriorated and the operator took no corrective action; revamp DPR planned, tender 'to be floated soon', no completion date. Press claims of a November 2024 full shutdown and partial resumption at 20 MLD could not be verified in any citable source and are excluded.

Madras High Court appoints Justice K.R. Shriram (retired, former Chief Justice of the Madras HC) as sole arbitrator over the disputes under the Bulk Water Purchase Agreement of 13 September 2005. The dispute is now in arbitration; still no dated commitment for restoring north Chennai's 100 MLD. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 still lists Minjur at 100 MLD with no mention of the termination.

commitments.title: Chennai Ring Main: 97.9 km bulk-water loop, construction June 2026 to May 2030
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu, ADB-financed (project 59311-001)
commitments.what: A closed loop of large-diameter mains around Greater Chennai connecting all major treatment plants and reservoirs, so any source can feed any zone at balanced pressure - billed as the first comprehensive ring main in an Indian city. CMWSSB's own environmental examination (March 2026) commits to construction from June 2026 to May 2030, a six-month trial, and commissioning by November 2030. Bids were opened 3 February 2026 and ADB approved a $230 million loan in early July 2026. The clock starts now; no contract-award announcement had surfaced as of this update.

commitment_source.label: CMWSSB Initial Environmental Examination for ADB, March 2026, para 49 (construction Jun 2026 - May 2030, trial to Nov 2030)

status_history.note: ADB approves a $230 million loan for the project (170+ km of water and sewer pipelines, 7 water pumping stations, 38 sewer pumping stations, 4.5 million beneficiaries). Cost figures on record conflict: Minister K.N. Nehru cited Rs 2,000 crore allocated (Mar 2025) and 'Rs 3,500 crore project' (Jul 2025) - likely allocation versus total, unresolved in sources.

commitments.title: 24x7 drink-from-tap supply in Kodambakkam and Adyar zones (Rs 1,958 crore)
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu (MAWS) / CMWSSB, with WATCO (Odisha) as nodal agency
commitments.what: Announced in the 2022-23 budget cycle: continuous pressurised drink-from-tap supply in Zone 10 (Kodambakkam) and Zone 13 (Adyar), modelled on Puri. The precursor - a Rs 69.64 crore pilot in Valasaravakkam - was promised complete by June 2023 in the government's own policy note. By March 2026 the single-ward trial was spoken of as done and work had begun in Besant Nagar, Adyar, Taramani and Thiruvanmiyur - but the two-zone rollout has never been given a public completion date. A rollout with no deadline cannot slip; that is itself the finding.

commitment_source.label: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.325 (Valasaravakkam pilot 'expected to be completed by June 2023'); CMWSSB-WATCO MoU week of 17-22 Jul 2023

status_history.note: Valasaravakkam pilot 'nearing completion' a month past its June 2023 due date; CMWSSB signs the implementation MoU with WATCO in the presence of Minister K.N. Nehru.

Valasaravakkam trial described as completed (exact commissioning date never published); 24x7 work under way in Besant Nagar, Adyar, Taramani and Thiruvanmiyur via the Pallipattu and Thiruvanmiyur distribution stations; Phase II to extend across Adyar zone and then Kodambakkam - no deadlines given.

commitments.title: Kosasthalaiyar basin storm drains: 588 km new + 175 km rehabilitated by December 2027
commitments.committed_by: Greater Chennai Corporation / Government of Tamil Nadu, ADB-financed (project 49107-009)
commitments.what: The $470.5 million integrated flood-management project for north Chennai's Kosasthalaiyar basin: 588 km of new storm drains, 175 km rehabilitated, channel improvements at Ambattur, Ariyallur, Kadappakkam and Korattur, to reduce flood exposure for 1.9 million people. ADB approved it on 23 September 2021 with project closing December 2027. GCC's own storm-water page (undated, apparently 2023-24 vintage) claimed 508 of 769 km complete with the balance 'by March 2024' - we found no dated confirmation that this happened, so the current position is honestly unverified.

commitment_source.label: ADB Project Administration Manual, Sept 2021 (closing Dec 2027); ADB approval 23 Sep 2021

status_history.note: GCC's storm-water page (undated; still live when accessed July 2026) reports 508 km of 769 km completed and promises the balance 'by March 2024' - a date long past on the page's own face. Note the scope arithmetic also differs: 588+175 = 763 km in the ADB manual versus 769 km on GCC's page. An ADB additional-financing line (49107-012) exists, indicating extension.
status_history.source_label: GCC storm-water department page (undated, accessed Jul 2026)

status_history.note: Ahead of the 2026 civic polls GCC claims 88% of storm-drain works finished city-wide (Rs 6,475 crore, 1,235 km over four years), while residents document missing links and recurring flooding. The project's ADB closing date of December 2027 has not yet lapsed; GCC's own March 2024 interim promise has.
status_history.source_label: Citizen Matters pre-poll report card, 13 Apr 2026

commitments.title: Kannankottai-Thervoy Kandigai reservoir (Chennai's fifth) by 2015
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / Water Resources Department (announced by CM J. Jayalalithaa, 2012)
commitments.what: A 1 TMC reservoir in Gummidipoondi taluk formed by combining two lakes, filled from the Kandaleru-Poondi (Krishna water) canal, adding ~65 MLD to Chennai. Announced in 2012, flagged off in 2013 with a 2015 target, it stalled within a year over land acquisition and then missed a string of announced ready-dates (three months away in Feb 2018; next month in Feb 2020) before being commissioned on 21 November 2020 - five years late. Cost: Rs 380 crore plus Rs 160 crore land; critics note it stores existing Krishna entitlement rather than adding new yield.

commitment_source.label: The News Minute, 1 Mar 2020 (announced 2012, work begun 2013, original target 2015); TN WRD dam page (completed 2020)

status_history.note: WRD says the reservoir will be 'ready in three months'. It was not.
Commissioned by Union Home Minister Amit Shah with CM Edappadi K. Palaniswami - five years after the original target. First reached full capacity 11 March 2021.

commitments.title: Mamallan reservoir, Kovalam basin (Chennai's sixth) - no completion date given
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / WRD (Budget 2025-26 announcement; foundation by CM M.K. Stalin)
commitments.what: A ~1.655 TMC drinking-water reservoir between OMR and ECR near Thiruporur, impounding surplus from 69 lakes of the Kovalam basin, meant to supply ~13 lakh people on the IT corridor and double as a flood buffer. Foundation stone laid 19 January 2026. No source states a completion date - for a reservoir this large, that absence is the trackable fact. Figures on record conflict: cost Rs 471 crore (pre-clearance, May 2025) versus Rs 342.60 crore (at foundation); supply 170 versus 120 MLD; area 4,375 versus 5,161 acres. The fishing community has opposed it, warning of livelihood losses.

commitment_source.label: The Print/PTI, 19 Jan 2026 (foundation stone, Rs 342.60 crore); announced in TN Budget 2025-26 per Deccan Chronicle

commitments.title: Desilt the four city reservoirs to restore 1.904 TMC of storage
commitments.what: Desilting Poondi, Cholavaram and Chembarambakkam (Rs 20.44 crore) plus Red Hills (Rs 9.90 crore) to restore ~1.904 TMC - roughly 45 days of city supply. An earlier post-2019-drought version (Rs 36 crore over eight years) 'never took off' per Arappor Iyakkam. The WRD Policy Note 2024-25 records the three-reservoir work 'under implementation' and Red Hills 'to be taken up shortly'; the Policy Note 2025-26 repeats that text verbatim a year later, with no completion date and no progress figures. The word-for-word carry-over across two budget cycles is itself the finding.

commitment_source.label: WRD Policy Note 2024-25, section 11.0, p.114; Rs 30.5 crore Assembly announcement by Minister Duraimurugan, 21 Jun 2024, per News Today

status_history.note: WRD Policy Note 2025-26, section 11.0 (p.79): the 2024-25 text repeats verbatim - Red Hills still 'to be taken up shortly', no date, no progress percentages. Entry date is approximate to the policy note's budget-session tabling.

commitments.title: Sholinganallur 54 MLD sewage treatment plant by January 2019
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB (funded under TNIPP, G.O.(Ms) No.51, MA&WS Dept, 18 Mar 2015)
commitments.what: An SBR plant (18 MLD Module-I + 36 MLD Module-II) serving the Pallikaranai and OMR belt, discharging to the Buckingham Canal. The contract was awarded to the DEE-TECH consortium on 3 March 2016 (Rs 134.44 crore, 30-month term), making the scheduled completion 10 January 2019. CMWSSB's own project sheet, dated 1 March 2022, records it 89% complete with September 2022 as the probable finish. The 36 MLD Module-II was finally inaugurated by CM Stalin on 5 February 2026 - about seven years late - with the state's 2025-26 policy note recording Module-I as 'completed and under trial run'. CMWSSB's sewerage page and projects list had not been updated to say so when checked in July 2026.

commitment_source.label: CMWSSB project sheet (contract 03.03.2016, 30-month term; progress as on 01.03.2022)

status_history.note: 89% complete three years past the contract date; CMWSSB's sheet gives September 2022 as the probable completion including trial runs.
status_history.source_label: CMWSSB project sheet, progress as on 01.03.2022

status_history.note: CM Stalin inaugurates the 36 MLD Sholinganallur plant (Module-II of this project) among Metro Water works worth Rs 635.31 crore - roughly seven years after the contract completion date. The MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 (section 5.3.4) records the 18 MLD Module-I as 'completed and under trial run'. CMWSSB's own sewerage page and projects list still showed the project as pending when accessed 5 Jul 2026.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 5 Feb 2026; MAWS Policy Note 2025-26, section 5.3.4

commitments.title: Raise Chennai's sewage treatment capacity to 951 MLD by 31 December 2021
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu (Additional Chief Secretary), in a sworn quarterly report to the NGT (OA 606/2018)
commitments.what: In its December 2020 quarterly compliance report to the National Green Tribunal, Tamil Nadu committed to raising Chennai's treatment capacity to 951 MLD by 31 December 2021 (Rs 636 crore of rehabilitation and new plants). It got there roughly two to three years late: the state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 records 957.80 MLD installed, with the Kodungaiyur I and II, Nesapakkam and Perungudi plants 'inaugurated by Hon'ble Chief Minister in 2023-24 & 2024-25 and in operation'. The residual finding is about transparency: CMWSSB's public sewerage page still said 745 MLD when accessed in July 2026, omitting every one of those new plants - the board's public face contradicts the state's own policy note by 200+ MLD.

commitment_source.label: TN Quarterly Report for December 2020 to NGT, OA 606/2018 (951 MLD by 31.12.2021)

status_history.note: NGT's order records TN's submission that Chennai's capacity 'attained' 912.80 MLD by October 2022 - ten months past the promise, still short of 951 - with a further 304 MLD committed (Rs 536.19 crore, AMRUT/TNIPP), no due date attached.
status_history.source_label: NGT order of 17 Nov 2022, OA 606/2018 (State of Tamil Nadu)

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 (section 5.3.2-5.3.3): installed capacity 957.80 MLD, with Kodungaiyur I & II (120+120), Nesapakkam (50) and Perungudi (60) 'inaugurated by Hon'ble Chief Minister in 2023-24 & 2024-25 and in operation'. The 951 MLD promise was met roughly 2-3 years late; exact inauguration dates were not published, only fiscal years. Entry date approximates the policy note's tabling.

The transparency residue: CMWSSB's public sewerage page, fetched this date, still says 'the present capacity of the treatment plant is 745 MLD' and its plant table omits all four new NGT-era plants. The board's public page contradicts the state's own policy note by more than 200 MLD.
status_history.source_label: CMWSSB Sewerage System page, accessed 5 Jul 2026

commitments.title: Eco-restoration of the Cooum (32 km, ~60 sub-projects)
commitments.committed_by: Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust (CRRT) / Government of Tamil Nadu
commitments.what: The Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project has run since 2015 (administrative sanction Rs 735.08 crore; in 2017 CRRT hoped to complete in three years, i.e. ~2020). The state's own status report to the NGT (as on 30 June 2021) carried sub-project deadlines through 2021-22 for sewage interception, modular STPs and resettlement. By June 2024, Rs 735 crore had been spent, 37 of 118 identified sewage outfalls were plugged, and 13,481 of 14,257 families resettled. The scoreboard that matters is CPCB's: after nine years and Rs 735 crore, the Cooum from Poonamallee to Central Jail remains a Priority I polluted river stretch - the worst class - with maximum BOD of 180 mg/l at Arumbakkam in CPCB's October 2025 assessment (2022-23 data). No revised whole-project deadline has been published.

commitment_source.label: Citizen Matters, 22 Sep 2017 (CRRT: three phases, hoping to complete 'in three years'); CRRT Cooum restoration page (sanction Rs 735.08 crore)

status_history.note: TN's status report to the NGT (OA 265/2016 SZ) sets sub-deadlines: CMWSSB interception packages by 30 Sep 2021, modular STPs at Chetpet/Nungambakkam/Maduravoyal through 2021, Langs Garden 10 MLD by May 2022, resettlement of the remaining 1,955 families by Sep 2021. Package IX (NSK Nagar) shelved due to encroachments.
status_history.source_label: TN status report on river restoration, NGT OA 265/2016(SZ), progress as on 30.06.2021

status_history.note: In January 2023 TNPCB found the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal 'dead' - no dissolved oxygen at 18 locations on the Cooum (23 on the Adyar). The same month, CPCB's polluted-river-stretches report (2019-21 data) recorded the Cooum's BOD at 345 mg/l, the highest of 603 rivers assessed nationally.
status_history.source_label: Citizen Matters, 23 Feb 2023 (TNPCB finding); DT Next, 31 Jan 2023 (CPCB report)

status_history.note: Rs 735 crore spent since 2015; 37 of the 118 outfalls in CRRT's initial enumeration plugged (Rs 193.25 crore), 23 more being plugged at Rs 50 crore. The 118 understates the problem: by December 2025, Citizen Matters reported ~900 discharge points into the Cooum and its feeder canals yet to be plugged.
status_history.source_label: Ground Report, 10 Jun 2024; Citizen Matters, 4 Dec 2025 (~900 discharge points)

status_history.note: CPCB's updated Polluted River Stretches assessment (October 2025, on 2022-23 data): the Cooum from Poonamallee to near Central Jail is a Priority I stretch - CPCB's worst class - with station BODs of 45 (Poonamallee), 121 (Anna Nagar), 180 (Arumbakkam), 156 (Amanjikarai), 74 (College Road), 91 (Napier Bridge) and 110 mg/l (Central Jail) against the 3 mg/l bathing criterion. An improvement on the 345 of 2019-21 (it is no longer the national worst - Mumbai's Mithi at Mahim is, at 210), and still Priority I. In June 2026 the Centre gave in-principle approval to Rs 7,500 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund for the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal - the next money, atop the spent Rs 735 crore.
status_history.source_label: CPCB, Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality - 2025 (Oct 2025 updated version)

commitments.title: Adyar river restoration (42 km, Rs 744.60 crore) - then repackaged at Rs 1,500 crore
commitments.committed_by: Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust (CRRT) / Government of Tamil Nadu
commitments.what: Works began in 2018 under a Rs 744.60 crore sanction. No overall completion date was ever published, so the due date here is the latest sub-deadline in the state's own status report to the NGT (Anakaputhur and Pammal UGSS, expected May 2023) - we label that derivation openly. In January 2023 TNPCB found zero dissolved oxygen at 23 locations on the river. The restoration was then repackaged: a Rs 1,500 crore 'One River, One Operator' PPP under a hybrid-annuity DBFOT model, whose CMWSSB concessionaire tender closed 30 November 2023 and which has featured in successive state budgets from 2024-25 (Rs 300 crore in 2025-26). No concession award had surfaced by July 2026, CRRT's page still shows the old Rs 744.60 crore frame, and whether the new money supersedes or adds to the old is not publicly documented. CPCB's October 2025 assessment keeps the Adyar in Priority I, its worst class.

commitment_source.label: TN status report on river restoration, NGT OA 265/2016(SZ), progress as on 30.06.2021 (works initiated 2018; packages due 2021-23); CRRT Adyar page

status_history.note: BOD 40 mg/l; 67 sewage outfalls; TNPCB finds zero dissolved oxygen at 23 locations (Jan 2023); fencing at 13.15 of 24.67 km; ~5,000 families still to relocate.

TN Budget 2024-25 features the Rs 1,500 crore Adyar restoration as a PPP - a fresh promise atop the unfinished one, with no completion dates. The underlying 'One River, One Operator' concessionaire tender had already closed on 30 November 2023; no award has been reported since (checked July 2026).
status_history.source_label: The South First, 19 Feb 2024; tender record via Projects Today

status_history.note: CPCB's updated Polluted River Stretches assessment (October 2025, on 2022-23 data): the Adyar from Ekkattuthangal to near Boat Club remains a Priority I stretch - CPCB's worst class - with maximum BOD 62 mg/l, seven years after works began. In June 2026 the Centre gave in-principle approval to Rs 7,500 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund covering the Adyar, Cooum and Buckingham Canal.
status_history.source_label: CPCB, Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality - 2025 (Oct 2025 updated version)

commitments.title: Buckingham Canal: demarcate in 6 months, then clear encroachments in 1 year (Madras HC, 12 Sept 2022)
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / PWD-WRD / Greater Chennai Corporation, under Madras High Court order in W.P.No.6609 of 2014
commitments.what: On 12 September 2022 the Madras High Court's First Bench (Chief Justice Munishwar Nath Bhandari and Justice N. Mala) ordered the canal's boundaries demarcated within six months - 'under no circumstance, the time line will be extended' - and encroachments removed within one year of demarcation completing. The demarcation deadline expired around March 2023 with about 40% done; because demarcation was never completed, the one-year encroachment clock never even began to run. In November 2024 the state announced it was abandoning restoration components in Chepauk-Triplicane and Mylapore for lack of funds. The canal's carrying capacity is down from 5,600 to 2,850 cusecs, the MRTS line itself the major encroacher. In June 2026 the Centre gave in-principle approval to Rs 7,500 crore for the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal under the Urban Challenge Fund - money that may restart works, but no evidence yet that the court-ordered demarcation was ever completed.

commitment_source.label: Madras HC, Kasthuribha and Indira Nagar Residents Welfare Forum v. Secretary PWD, W.P.No.6609 of 2014, order 12 Sep 2022 (full text on Indian Kanoon)

status_history.note: Demarcation deadline (~Mar 2023) long lapsed at ~40% done (northern and southern stretches); the contingent encroachment-removal year never started. In Nov 2024 GoTN announced abandoning restoration components in Chepauk-Triplicane and Mylapore 'due to a severe shortage of funds'. A WRD DPR of Oct 2023 had priced the work at Rs 1,696.5 crore.

PWD/WRD floats a fresh Rs 2,388 crore proposal for the 167 km Pazhaverkadu-Marakkanam stretch - a new plan, not a resumption of the abandoned one; the state sought Rs 20 crore from the Centre just for the DPR.

The Centre gives in-principle approval for Rs 7,500 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund for reviving the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal, phase one of the CM's Integrated Urban Transformation Mission. In-principle only - DPRs are still to be submitted in stages - and no evidence the court-ordered demarcation was completed. Status stays stalled on the HC order; the funding picture has changed.

commitments.title: Restore the Kodungaiyur 45 MLD recycled-water plant to full output in 18 months
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB, via PPP contract with VA Tech Wabag
commitments.what: Chennai built two 45 MLD tertiary treatment (TTRO) plants to sell recycled water to industry. By the government's own 2023 policy note they were running at 23 MLD (Kodungaiyur) and 15 MLD (Koyambedu). In March 2026 CMWSSB awarded Wabag a refurbish-finance-operate-transfer contract reported at over Rs 1,000 crore to bring Kodungaiyur back to its full 45 MLD within 18 months, plus 18.5 years of operation. That a plant commissioned in 2019 needs a four-figure-crore refurbishment seven years on is itself part of the record.

commitment_source.label: Indian Chemical News, 14 Mar 2026 (Wabag PPP award, 18-month restoration); underperformance per MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.318

update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked against a small calendar of documents: the MAWS Policy Note each April (the single richest source of CMWSSB's own targets), ADB project documents for the ring main and Kosasthalaiyar drains, and CMWSSB/ministerial announcements reported in DT Next and The Hindu. Each commitment carries a next-check date; a passed next-check with no new citation is itself flagged, never silently updated.
sources_note: Sources are the institutions' own documents wherever they exist (MAWS Policy Notes, CMWSSB board policy, ADB loan documents, contractor releases) and dated reporting where they do not. Where figures conflict (Perur's two costs, the ring main's two price tags, drain kilometres) both are shown with their labels. Claims we could not verify - the Minjur November 2024 shutdown, the Kosasthalaiyar completion - are named as unverified rather than silently dropped.
